implementation_notes: Go has no `goto` into a block and only one loop construct, so lexical spaghetti is rarer; the Go-specific tangle is `panic`/`recover` used to escape a loop, which turns the panic machinery into a nonlocal jump and defeats the point of panics, and deeply nested `if`/`err != nil` chains whose error paths end in a single fallback that swallows the distinction. The idiomatic reformulation of the error tangle is to handle each error where it is raised and use named results plus a deferred cleanup, which makes the error path visible instead of funnelled. `gocyclo`/`gocognit` report the complexity; `go vet` reports none of this.
idiom_name: panic/recover used as a break; deep if/else with unlabeled break
pitfalls: Named return values plus deferred modification make the real exit path invisible at a glance.
`err` shadowing inside nested blocks is the Go equivalent of flag-driven branching and produces errors that are checked in the wrong order.
`select` inside a loop with several cases is a legitimate state machine written by hand; adding a `default` to it can turn it into a spin loop.
